- Top concerns raised: SOC 2 status, telemetry/what we collect by default in the Console, cookie usage on docs site and admin console, data residency options.

4) Product question (for Dev): we flagged telemetry cookie behaviour in the Console and docs — Alice, you asked whether any third-party trackers are present in the admin console. Short answer: none by default, but I'll loop in our engineering lead for the details.

Marissa / Karthik / Alice — quick technical answers to seed the workbook. I kept this high level; happy to expand or hop on the 10:00 PT slot.

Telemetry collected by the Console (defaults):
- Event types: admin UI interactions (route, action), API request/response metadata, platform errors.
- Fields captured: timestamp, tenant_id (customer id), user_id (internal admin id), request_id, api_key_hash (non-reversible hash), HTTP method, URL path (no request body by default), response_status, latency_ms, error_code.
- Network identifiers: we capture source IP for security logs only and it is redacted in analytics exports by default. IP is encrypted at rest and access-controlled; retention default is 90 days for hosted.
- Cookies: Admin console sets a session cookie (secure, httpOnly) for auth and a short-lived CSRF token cookie. We do NOT load third-party analytics in the admin console by default. Our public docs site includes optional analytics (Google Analytics) but that is opt-in per-account and can be disabled for Enterprise/Dedicated customers.

PII & GDPR notes:
- We do not log request bodies or document contents by default in the hosted runtime telemetry stream. Ingestion traces are only kept if customers opt in for debugging; when retained they are masked for known PII patterns and available only to SRE with Just-In-Time access.
- Data residency: Hosted stores telemetry in the region selected for the account (us-west / eu-west options). Dedicated/Private customers can keep telemetry in their VPC/on-prem stack.
- Right-to-be-forgotten: we support deletion APIs that cascade to telemetry exports and analytics within the retention windows; for Hosted accounts full deletion requires a support ticket to ensure backfilled caches are cleared.

HIPAA / BAA:
- Redwood can sign a BAA for Dedicated and Private deployments today. For Hosted customers we have a process to evaluate BAA requests; in some cases we offer contract amendments and limited-scoped BAA coverage for production-controlled data. Grace will follow up on exact contract language.

Attachments / references:
- Link: https://redwood.app/secure/docs/telemetry-retention (technical doc)
- SOC2 summary has auditor/contact info — see attached PDF (Redwood_SOC2_Summary_2025.pdf). If you need the bridge letter we can request it from ComplyAudit (auditor).
